taxonomy_note: Workflow routing only. Choose final root-cause taxonomy from supported evidence.

controls.boundary: Audit query scope across partition expansion, cursor and export publication
controls.source_trace: Follow a caller query into effective log scope and serializer fields. Differentiate read access to security events from permission to read credentials/PII inside them.
controls.implementation_branch: Evaluate reader scope, query filters, export jobs and fields independently from permission to perform the logged actions. Audit readers may intentionally see security-relevant cross-user metadata; establish which contents remain protected. A redacted UI does not prove raw export/search restrictions, and a permitted event count is not automatically a complete log disclosure.
controls.operational_method: Specialize in audit query/export scope carried across the UI, query DSL, cursor and async result link. Retain the immutable tenant/project scope attached to the reader capability and compare it with index/partition selection and field projection after query rewriting. Test a scoped synthetic search, a forged continuation/export context and the final redacted event payload. Ordinary one-object API access without audit query fan-out belongs in generic object/property review.
controls.controlled_verification: Query synthetic audit events through a scoped reader capability, then alter the continuation/export query or partition while preserving the same visible filter. Inspect final event fields and artifact audience against the immutable scope.
controls.false_positive_discriminator: An audit-event count or event type may be intentionally visible; require an actual field/object policy violation.
controls.remediation_acceptance: Constrain reader scope and redact unnecessary sensitive fields, preserving authorized incident response and audit fidelity.
